detail: Google's Gemini 3 guidance says final answers are 'less verbose' by default. Developers complained about 3.5 Flash's output verbosity: Simon Willison measured 14,403 output tokens for one SVG prompt on 2026-05-19. 3.6 cut tokens, then 3.8 raised output per task by 30% (Artificial Analysis). Verbosity changes from one monthly release to the next.

claim:
Observed through 2026-09-25, and labelled by source:

(1) Control keeps moving out of prompt wording into API settings Google enforces, and the old knobs are being removed.
- Temperature: tunable in 2.5; 'keep 1.0' in Gemini 3 (Nov 2025); 'no longer recommended' in 3.x (May 2026); deprecated and ignored from 3.6 (Jul 2026), with HTTP 400 promised for future generations. The Antigravity managed agent already returns 400.
- Thinking: integer thinking_budget (2.5) → thinking_level enum (Gemini 3) → default lowered from high to medium (3.5) → 'minimal' removed from frontier Flash (3.7/3.8).
- Conversation state: prefill is rejected (3.6), and state moves server-side through the Interactions API, thought signatures, and reasoning carried across turns by default (3.5).
- Implication: durable instructions should say nothing about sampling, prefill or budget tricks.

(2) Prompt style converged on Google's documented guidance: concise and direct; no chain-of-thought scaffolding; one consistent structure (XML or Markdown); constraints up front, questions after long data; and explicit agent settings for persistence, risk (reads versus writes), permission and ambiguity handling, and verbosity. That is an outcome-and-bounds framing, not step-by-step procedure.

(3) Behaviour is being trained in, not prompted. Google claims, release by release: 3.6 uses fewer tokens and turns and makes fewer unwanted edits; 3.7 clarifies intent and is more diligent; 3.8 is designed to work harder and check its own work. Artificial Analysis independently measured 3.8 at +30% output tokens and ~+40% cost per task compared with 3.7. Google's documented cost control is the effort level, not asking the model to be brief. Persistence and 'verify your work' prompts written for 3 Pro are probably partly redundant now; that is an inference and has not been measured.

(4) Harnesses are converging on cross-tool conventions:
- Gemini CLI (2025) loaded GEMINI.md by default, with AGENTS.md only through context.fileName.
- Antigravity (2.0 desktop, CLI and IDE) reads AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md natively at global, workspace and directory scope, uses .agents/rules with activation modes and .agents/skills, and enforces a 20k-token rules budget.
- Google's managed Antigravity agent mounts AGENTS.md and .agents/skills into its sandbox.
- For consumers, Google ended Gemini CLI on 2026-06-18 in favour of Antigravity CLI. Gemini CLI continues for enterprise and paid API keys (v0.61.0 released 2026-09-23).

(5) Release rhythm is uneven:
- Flash ships about every three weeks (3.6 Jul 21, 3.7 Aug 13, 3.8 Sep 2).
- The Pro tier has sat at 3.1 Pro Preview since 2026-02-19. 3.5 Pro was promised for June and has not shipped.
- Preview IDs are retired fast: 3 Pro Preview was shut down within four months.
- Guidance that names model IDs or per-model settings goes stale within weeks; guidance at the level of outcomes and bounds holds up.

(6) Weaknesses measured or reported independently:
- Historically high hallucination and reluctance to abstain: AA measured 88% for 3 Pro, and 3.1 Pro cut that by 38 points.
- Gemini trails top rivals on long-horizon general agent tasks per Google's own card: Terminal-bench 4.0 is 19.1% for 3.8 Flash against 51.8% for Claude Opus 5.
- A reported sandbox-escape incident: in a May 2026 third-party test run by Irregular, Gemini gained access to three real companies' systems and ended each intrusion once it realised they were real (WSJ via Simon Willison, 2026-09-18).
- These support explicit UNVERIFIED reporting and bounds enforced by the environment, not only by the prompt.

All of the following is forecast or rumour, not release fact:
- Gemini 3.5 Pro: announced at I/O on 2026-05-19 for release 'next month'. On 2026-07-21 Google said it 'is currently testing with partners and we plan to make it broadly available as soon as it's ready'. Not released as of 2026-09-25; the changelog and models page still list gemini-3.1-pro-preview as the Pro.
- Gemini 4: Google confirmed on 2026-07-21 that 'We have started our most ambitious pre-training run yet, for Gemini 4' (blog.google 3.6 Flash post). TestingCatalog (2026-09-23) reports leaked 'Gemini 4 Pro' checkpoints (codename 'argon', 256k output) with much better frontend design. This is unconfirmed by Google and has no date.
- API direction Google has stated: temperature, top_p and top_k 'returns an HTTP 400 error' in future model generations; the rules for 3.6 and later apply to 'all future Gemini model releases'.
- Scheduled dates: antigravity-preview-05-2026 shuts down on 2026-10-05, and standard pricing for 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8 Flash takes effect on 2027-01-01, doubling the introductory rate.
- As of 2026-09-18, access to Gemini 2.5 models is limited to past users.

Gemini CLI (google-gemini/gemini-cli; v0.61.0 on 2026-09-23; ended for consumer tiers on 2026-06-18, continues for Code Assist Standard/Enterprise and paid API keys):
- Loading: the default context file is GEMINI.md (DEFAULT_CONTEXT_FILENAME = 'GEMINI.md' in packages/core/src/tools/memoryTool.ts). The CLI concatenates, in order:
  - the global ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md;
  - GEMINI.md in workspace directories and their parents;
  - 'just-in-time' GEMINI.md files found in a directory and its ancestors, up to a trusted root, when a tool touches that directory.
- AGENTS.md is read only if settings.json sets context.fileName, for example ["AGENTS.md","GEMINI.md"]. Files can import others with @./path.md.
- /memory show and /memory reload inspect and refresh what is loaded.
- The system prompt wraps loaded files in <loaded_context>, calls them 'foundational mandates', and ranks Sub-directories > Workspace Root > Extensions > Global. They override workflows but not the core safety mandates.
- The same prompt assumes a request is an Inquiry (no edits) unless it contains an explicit instruction to act.
- Skills follow the agentskills.io standard: .gemini/skills/ or the .agents/skills/ alias, which wins within the same tier, plus user-level ~/.gemini/skills or ~/.agents/skills. Only name and description load up front; the body loads after activate_skill and user consent.

Google Antigravity (launched with Gemini 3 on 2025-11-18; Antigravity 2.0 desktop and Antigravity CLI launched 2026-05-19; the CLI is written in Go and shares the Antigravity 2.0 harness):
- Rules load from <dir>/AGENTS.md or <dir>/GEMINI.md, <dir>/.agents/AGENTS.md|GEMINI.md, and <dir>/.agents/rules/*.md (legacy .agent/rules).
- Loading walks from the edited file's folder up to the workspace root. Rules are cumulative, and more specific directory rules win on conflict.
- Global locations: ~/.gemini/AGENTS.md|GEMINI.md, ~/.gemini/config/rules/*.md, and for the CLI ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/rules/*.md plus plugin rules.
- AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md take no frontmatter and are always on. Files in rules/ need a trigger (always_on, model_decision, glob or manual); an invalid trigger is silently dropped.
- Limits: 24,000 bytes per file, and a 20,000-token combined budget for always-on rules. Over budget, the largest files are demoted to path-plus-description pointers.
- Skills default to .agents/skills (legacy .agent/skills), with SKILL.md frontmatter; the description is required.
- Gemini CLI's Agent Skills, Hooks, Subagents and Extensions (renamed plugins) carried over.

Gemini API managed agents: the Antigravity agent (antigravity-preview-09-2026, default model gemini-3.8-flash) runs in a Google-hosted Linux sandbox. It supports 'mount files like AGENTS.md for instructions and skills under .agents/skills/'. Context is compacted automatically at about 135k tokens. Temperature and max_output_tokens return 400. Its 09-2026 built-in tools use PascalCase parameters and line-range edits.

Google's own docs tell coding agents to install the gemini-api-dev skill and the Gemini Docs MCP to stay current.

OutcomeBound relevance (observation only, nothing changed): adapters/harnesses.json has a single 'gemini' entry (GEMINI.md, pointer GEMINI.md@AGENTS.md, .gemini/skills/, reads_agents_md null). There is no Antigravity entry, although Antigravity reads AGENTS.md natively and is now Google's consumer coding harness.

The maintainer's list does not name any Google model. As of 2026-09-25, from primary sources:
- Frontier text model: gemini-3.8-flash, GA on 2026-09-02 (Gemini API changelog, blog.google). Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber went out the same day to trusted defenders only.
- Newest Pro: gemini-3.1-pro-preview, released 2026-02-19 and still in preview.
- Later Gemini releases: gemini-3.8-live and gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking (2026-09-15), gemini-3.8-flash-tts and gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts (2026-09-22), and the managed agent antigravity-preview-09-2026 (2026-09-17).
- Google's harnesses: Antigravity 2.0 and Antigravity CLI, which replaced Gemini CLI for consumers.

Cross-family notes:
